description: Snowflake lateral column aliases in a SELECT list that does NOT go through ProjectOperator: a select item may reference the alias of an EARLIER item of the same list. The plain projection path always supported this; two others did not, because each projects the SELECT list itself. Every GROUPED path - plain GROUP BY, GROUP BY ALL, positional ordinals, ROLLUP / CUBE / GROUPING SETS and implicit whole-relation aggregation - evaluated each item against a representative group row with no sibling-alias context, so the derived item silently came out NULL; and a WINDOWED projection failed the whole query with 'Column not found'. The rule has a rejecting half a plain GROUP BY now enforces the way Snowflake does: only EARLIER aliases are visible, so naming a later item's alias is 'invalid identifier', and because a real COLUMN outranks a same-named alias, an item reading a column that is neither grouped nor aggregated fails to compile. The permissive shapes are pinned beside them - star items, correlated subqueries, GROUP BY ALL, super-groups against the UNION of their grouping sets, an expression key matched across formatting and an AS-less alias, and a date-part keyword that must not be read as a column. On a super-group's subtotal row the NULLed dimension must NULL its derived siblings too, not carry the representative row's value. An alias inside an aggregate's ARGUMENT means the alias's defining EXPRESSION evaluated per row, not its per-group value. Converted 1:1 from query/GroupByLateralAliasTest (now retired); the Java read individual row indexes and, for the super-group cases, looped over rows checking a relationship, which the converted tests state as whole ordered row sets.
